brief:
Two things before the numbers, and the first one is the biggest thing in your log.

You have not trained legs in fifteen days. Your last leg day was Legs A on 20 August, and Legs B was 16 August, nineteen days ago. Since then you have run five sessions and every one of them was push or pull: Push B, Pull B, Push A, Pull A, Push B. The six-day order has been turning over correctly on paper, but the leg days keep getting replaced. My program trainer flagged this and it is the largest fact in the whole review. With the show on 1 March, legs are not the part you can carry on someone else's numbers. The app will offer you Pull B tonight because that is where the order sits. If you want tonight to be a leg day instead, the plan screen lets you set the day by hand and the order continues from there. That is your call, not mine, but you should be making it on purpose rather than by default.

Second: on 2 September you wrote "New gym. No smith machine." Pull B opens with the Smith Bent-Over Row. If you are back at your usual gym, that card is right and you earned it — you took all four rungs to ten reps on 25 August, so the whole ramp goes up five pounds and finishes at 155. If you are still at the new place, that row does not exist for you and neither does the number. Do the closest row you can get to, log what you actually lift, and the app will learn from that. I would rather say this now than let you find out at the rack.

And I need one answer from you: is the new gym now your gym, or were you passing through? Your chest press has been logged at three different scales in twelve days — 165 to 180 at your usual place, 67.5 to 75 on the Hammer Strength on 23 August, and 97.5 to 157.5 on 2 September. Those are three different machines wearing one name. If the new gym is permanent, the right move is to re-baseline the program there rather than have me keep quoting weights from a building you have left. Tell me and I will do it properly.

Tonight's numbers, if you run Pull B. Two lifts that had been stuck finally move. Your incline curl goes to 30-pound dumbbells for two sets of eight: now that it is two sets rather than three, both surviving sets hit ten at 25 every single time, which is the top of the range and exactly what was being masked by the third set. Your cable reverse curl goes to 38.75 — that is 37.5 plus one of the small add-on weights — for three sets of ten, because you have done eleven, eleven, eleven at 37.5 twice running and asking for a twelfth rep has failed both times. Face pulls go to 30 for two sets of twelve, off 27.5 for fifteen and fifteen on 28 August.

Three hold their weight and ask for reps instead. Close-grip pulldown stays at 127.5 and wants ten on all three — your third set fell to eight last time and that is the only thing between you and 135. Straight-arm pulldown stays at 45 and wants twelve, one more than the eleven you have hit three times. Shrugs stay at 80 and want thirteen.

Housekeeping. Your review did not run yesterday, 3 September — the machine that runs it had a broken setup, now fixed, and no numbers were affected. Your bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August; with the show six months out that trend is the one number I cannot get from anywhere else, so step on the scale this week. Easy cardio twice this week, twenty to thirty minutes.

Meso 2, week 2 of 4, a build block. All three trainers reported today; two disagreements, both settled, and no objections raised on safety grounds.

proposals.why: The cable lateral raise is the only side-delt work on Push A and it has drifted to seventh of eight — on 27 August the session ended after the sixth exercise, so your side delts got nothing that night while your rear delts got all three sets; this moves it up to fifth, straight after the shoulder press, so it happens before the tail of the session rather than after it.

overrides.reason: On 25 August you hit ten reps — the top of the range — on all four rungs at 115, 135, 145 and 150, so the whole ramp goes up five pounds. If there is no smith machine where you are tonight, this card does not apply: do the nearest row you can and log that instead.
The weight stays at 127.5 because your third set dropped to eight last time even after a full two minutes' rest. Ten on all three is what buys 135, and this machine's next step is a full 7.5.
Eleven, eleven and eleven at 45 on 25 August — one rep short of the top of the range on every set, so tonight asks for the twelfth before it asks for more weight.
Twelve, twelve and twelve at 80 is the bottom of the range on your first outing at that weight, so this asks thirteen at the same dumbbells rather than repeating twelve.

Now that this is two sets instead of three, both remaining sets have hit ten at 25 every time — the top of the range — and it was only the third set that ever fell short. That earns the next dumbbell up, so 30 for two sets of eight.

Eleven, eleven, eleven at 37.5 on both 15 and 25 August. Asking for a twelfth rep has failed twice, so instead this adds the smallest weight the machine owns — one 1.25 add-on, making 38.75 — and re-enters at ten.
On 28 August you did 27.5 for fifteen and fifteen, the top of the range on both sets, so this steps up by the small add-on weight to 30 and re-enters at twelve.

dissent.progression: All four rungs hit ten reps on 25 August, so the whole ramp earns +5 and tops at 155.
dissent.recovery: Hold — his 2 September note says the new gym has no smith machine, so a carried-over smith number may describe equipment he cannot reach.
dissent.why: Recovery is right about the risk and wrong about the remedy. If there is no smith machine tonight then 150 and 155 are equally unusable, so holding buys him nothing; if there is one, he earned the step cleanly by taking every rung to the top of the range. The hold would cost him a real session to guard against a problem it does not actually solve. I took the earned numbers and put the equipment doubt where it can do some good — on the card itself, in the notice bar, and as a direct question about whether the new gym is now his gym.

dissent.progression: 27.5 for fifteen and fifteen on 28 August is the top of the range on both sets, which earns the +2.5 add-on to 30.
dissent.recovery: Keep 27.5 and ask for fifteen, because the Pull B record shows only twelves.
dissent.why: Face pulls are the same rope on the same stack whichever day they fall on, so the newest clean performance is what counts, and that is 28 August at fifteen and fifteen. The twelves recovery points to are from 25 August, three days older — and recovery itself showed that night's second set was timestamped nearly a full day later, meaning it was typed in after the fact rather than lifted. I am not ruling against recovery's concern about set counts; that concern is about a third set Pull B no longer has.
